column2: The standard format every input is normalized into, so a Telegram message and a cron job are handled by identical downstream logic.
Message, scheduled, webhook, and heartbeat.
Internal runtime signal, every 30 minutes by default, that triggers a light self-check and queued background work; it needs no external reply.
Direct-message setting per channel: allowlist (only IDs in allowFrom), open (anyone who finds the bot), or disabled.
Group-chat setting per channel: mention (respond only when @mentioned), all (process every message), or disabled.
Use platform user IDs (numeric Telegram IDs, Slack member IDs), never usernames or display names, because those can change.
Recommended webhook method: the caller signs each payload with a shared secret. Unlike a bearer token, the signature is bound to the content.
One event at a time per session. Prevents races in tool calls and memory writes, but a slow tool call blocks later events.
Assembly steps 1-7: identity files, MEMORY.md, daily logs, tool schemas. Unchanged between turns in a session, so it can be prompt-cached.
Session history plus the incoming event. Grows each turn and is not cached, so volatile content belongs at the end.
Governing workspace file size. The book's ungoverned six-month example costs about $165/month in input tokens versus about $13 governed.
Absent context files are skipped without error. An AGENTS.md startup check can turn a missing SOUL.md into an explicit alert.
Keep secrets out of every context file, since the model can read all of it. Put them in environment variables used by tool code.
How the agent communicates, what wins when values conflict, what it will never do, and how it handles ambiguous instructions.
Operational runbook: files to load at session start, safety defaults, confirmation rules, memory governance, group chat and tool/channel policies.
On an edge-case conflict, SOUL.md wins because it sets the frame the model uses to interpret everything else.
Ordered list of alternate models tried in sequence when the primary is unavailable from rate limits, outages, or budget caps.
A directory under skills/ holding a SKILL.md (description, input schema, behavioral notes) plus the implementation code.
Schema validation, permission check, sandbox check, execution, result normalization.
Behavioral notes are read by the model, not checked by the execution layer. Put high-stakes constraints in the tool code as well.
Gates that name exact details (recipient, file path, event) remove the gap left when the model interprets a vague word like destructive.
A cheap model summarizes large tool output before it enters context, so later calls carry a short summary instead of the full payload.
Session history (current conversation), daily logs in memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md, and curated long-term MEMORY.md.
MEMORY.md facts that were true when written but are now outdated; the model still acts on them confidently. Dating entries makes drift visible.
Setting channel to null runs a task with no external message, which suits housekeeping such as the daily log write.
